title: Fermionic Lattice Supersolidity in the Attractive Three-Color Fermi-Hubbard Model
abstract: The recent experimental realization of the half-filled three-color Fermi-Hubbard model on a square optical lattice provides a novel platform for exploring exotic states of matter beyond conventional SU(2) systems. In this Letter, we investigate the three-color Fermi-Hubbard model with color-dependent attractive interactions using determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations. We find that, at quantum degenerate temperatures, a lattice Fermi supersolid state emerges from the interplay between a moderately-to-strongly interacting two-color subsystem and a weakly coupled third-color environment. This supersolid state, characterized by the coexistence of charge-density-wave and color-superfluid orders, is highly promising for experimental detection with current techniques. Our results demonstrate that the attractive three-color Fermi-Hubbard model on a square optical lattice offers an experimentally accessible system for exploring the supersolidity of ultracold lattice fermions, requiring only a simple lattice geometry and easily tunable onsite interactions.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates supersolid states in the three-color Fermi-Hubbard model using DQMC simulations. It demonstrates that a stable supersolid phase emerges from the interplay between two strongly interacting colors and a weakly coupled third color. This offers an experimentally accessible platform for realizing and studying coexisting crystalline and superfluid orders in ultracold fermions.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence and characteristics of a lattice Fermi supersolid state in an attractive three-color Fermi-Hubbard model.
main_result: A stable Fermi supersolid phase, characterized by the coexistence of charge-density-wave (CDW) and color-superfluid (CSF) orders, is found due to weak coupling between two interacting colors and a third weakly coupled environment.
method: The research employs Determinant Quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations alongside mean-field theory calculations for analyzing order parameters and phase boundaries.
model_or_system: The system is the attractive three-color Fermi-Hubbard model realized on a square optical lattice, studied at half-filling. The Hamiltonian includes color-dependent attractions ($U_{\alpha eta} < 0$).
key_observables: Charge Density Wave (CDW) Order Parameter ($D_{123}$), Color-Superfluid (CSF) Correlation Ratio ($R_{CSF}$), and the CSF order parameter ($P_{CSF}$).
important_parameters: Interaction strengths $|U|$ and $|U'|$, quantum degenerate temperature ($T=1/12$), and lattice size dependence ($1/L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on DQMC simulations for finite-size scaling and mean-field theory by tracing out one color to simplify the Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing the SS region, plot order parameters vs. interaction strengths, and show finite-size extrapolations of CDW and CSF orders against $1/L$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical model and key observables to performing DQMC simulations to map out the phase diagram, followed by mean-field analysis to understand the competition between CDW and CSF orders.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses exotic quantum phases (supersolids) in systems relevant to ultracold atoms trapped in optical lattices, providing detailed theoretical predictions for experimental detection using color/spin degrees of freedom.
